findings.finding: A $3.0m senior secured convertible issued 2026-09-28 converts at 90% of the lowest 10-day VWAP into registered, freely tradable ADSs. At today's ~$4.8 that is roughly 650-700k ADSs against ~52k ADSs traded today, so the holder's conversion-and-sell flow continues through the 2026-09-30 session.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The note was issued one trading day before the window opens, and the conversion price resets down with each lower daily VWAP. That gives the holder every incentive to convert and sell continuously from the first days rather than later, so the 09-30 session's supply comes from a position that is at most 2 days old and >10x daily turnover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The two 2026 ADS ratio changes (07-14 and 09-10) were followed by falls of 13-25% on 07-15, 07-20, 07-24, 09-15, 09-16 and 09-28 (baseline history), and the 60-day run-up is -90.15%. Next closes after those falls alternated sign: -9.3, +0.5, -4.8, +17.5, -20.5, +12.2 and -16.5, so the line pushes down while the magnitude is noisy.
findings.why_not_priced: The close holds what has been sold so far (two days, about $0.5-0.6m of total turnover including every other seller). It does not hold the rest of a $3.0m convertible that can only be sold down at a discount to the market. If it had priced the remaining supply, the discount-to-VWAP conversion would give the holder no edge at the close and volume would have spiked. It did not: 1.06x.
findings.independence: The 1-for-20 ADS ratio change on 2026-09-10 and a 14.6-trillion-share incentive plan No. 2 adopted 2026-08-15 point to the same dilution machinery: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1806524/000121390026090989/ea0302341-6k_lion.htm
